Messages.Author: Legbiter
Messages.Body:
This came up in the post-tournament game.

It is Steve's untap. He has the succubus club.

Lunar and Legbiter are contesting the Labyrinth.

Legbiter offers to give Steve his copy of the contested card until Steve's
next untap. The idea is for Legbiter to avoid losing one pool. The
advantage to Steve is that he puts extra hurt on his prey Lunar, and by
essentially compelling her to yield the location, he helps his ally
Legbiter to hurt his predator Rob.

After much discussion we accepted John Eagle's ruling that this is
illegal. Our reasoning was that while cards are contested, NO-ONE controls
them, and if one does not control a card, it may not be traded.

Were we right?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Yes. Contested Cards are out of play except for being contested, and
cannot be affected by anything else (except explicit card text, of
course, like Praxis: Solomon).
